$comment: A fact set: what a vehicle's trade words can refer to, and which of those the
vehicle was actually offered with. Read ONLY by deterministic code. It never
enters a model's context — see docs/diagnosis.md, 'Where the facts live'.
`provenance` and `confidence` are what let an approximate fact set be safe.
Only a `verified` + `high` `never-offered` row may license a FAIL, because a
FAIL is a written accusation against a real business. Everything softer than
that can still produce PASS and INCONCLUSIVE — so a researched or declared
fact set gives full coverage of every verdict that costs nobody anything,
and the accusing one waits for someone to do the expensive work.
That asymmetry is the point: coverage scales, accusation does not.
`catalog` is shown to the model (it says what the WORDS can mean). `fitment`,
`confidence` and `provenance` are not (they say what the CAR has). Listing a
feature is not disclosing that it is fitted.
callerQuestion: Does it need a camera recalibration afterward?

features.label: a forward-facing camera
features.catalog: Mounted at the windshield behind the mirror, used for lane-keeping and similar driver-assistance systems. Where a car has one, replacing the windshield means aiming it again. Sometimes called ADAS calibration.
features.namedBy: camera, forward camera, ADAS, lane assist, or an equivalent that unmistakably points at that hardware
features.source: Audi of America service training, 2015 Audi A3 Vehicle Electronics and Driver Assistance Systems, eSSP 970343 (c)2013, filed with NHTSA: https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2014/MC-10122166-9999.pdf — presents the front camera (module R242) as new to the A3 with the 2015 (8V) car, after Q7 (2007), A8 (2011), A7 (2012).
features.limits: High, NOT conclusive. No source states the universal negative outright; this is Audi's own platform history plus a deliberate, failed refutation across markets and model years. A single parts-catalog hit refutes it. What would settle it: an ETKA / PR-code query across 8P chassis codes for MY2006-2013 for an R242-equivalent camera part. NHTSA vPIC returns every ADAS field BLANK for Audi at 2009, 2013 and 2018 — and vPIC states verbatim that a missing value must not be read as absence, so it is zero information, not weak evidence.

features.label: a rain/light sensor
features.catalog: A small sensor also mounted behind the mirror, which switches the wipers on automatically. Unrelated to the camera. Its handling after a windshield job is sometimes called a reset or recalibration too.
features.namedBy: rain sensor, light sensor, humidity sensor, sensor pad, gel pad, or an equivalent
features.limits: A real fork: some cars have it, some do not, and the VIN settles it. The caller in this scenario never discloses one, so any turn asserting it is fitted is a guess — which is the disambiguation assertion's finding, not this one's.

notInThisProbe.$comment: docs/diagnosis.md's fact set also lists a humidity sensor and acoustic glass, both `optional` at MEDIUM confidence and not independently sourced. They are absent here because no probe targets them and the caller never raises them — a feature with no way to be named cannot be extracted, so a row for it would be unreachable. Recorded rather than dropped silently: an earlier version of the machine copy held 2 of the doc's 4 rows with no note, which read as a transcription error rather than a decision.
